A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same δ-GClip research. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The experiment in v1 Appendix B is retained in v2's main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 and VAE/Fashion-MNIST experiments, including scheduling comparisons and the weight-decay ablation in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and reports additional Vision Transformer and DistilBERT results in Section 3.2 and Figures 5–6.

M1.justification: The deterministic and stochastic δ-GClip updates, including the lower step-size bound ηδ, are unchanged. The transformer experiments evaluate the existing optimizer on additional architectures without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds Quora sincere/insincere question classification, extending evaluation from image classification and image distribution learning to text classification. CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST remain; using a Vision Transformer on CIFAR-10 does not itself add dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The original SGD, Adam, and standard GClip comparisons are retained. v2 adds the combined Adam-plus-GClip comparator for DistilBERT in Figure 6; the Vision Transformer comparison uses the already evaluated Adam baseline.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 introduces distinct evaluation configurations: Vision Transformer training from random initialization and DistilBERT fine-tuning, including an η/γ search for the latter. These extend the experimental design; the existing ResNet/VAE batch sizes, hyperparameter grids, scheduling, and weight-decay settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The scheduling comparisons, small-δ comparisons, and weight-decay ablation are retained. v1 Appendix B becomes v2 Figure 3 with the same plot and findings. The transformer additions are benchmark evaluations, not new ablation or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added transformer curves do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets: Figure 5 reports similar Vision Transformer loss and accuracy trajectories for δ-GClip and Adam, while Figure 6 reports comparable DistilBERT training loss and test accuracy against Adam-plus-GClip. These are new-setting results. All four original experiment plots retain identical graphical content.

T1.justification: The PL* definition, network assumptions, width/radius conditions, convergence bounds, and proofs remain substantively unchanged. Theorems 1.1–1.2 become 2.1–2.2, preparatory lemmas move to Section 5, and Appendix A retains the same stochastic argument.

C1.justification: The central convergence and optimizer-competitiveness claims are retained. v2 extends the abstract's explicit empirical contribution to modern transformer architectures and also frames the novelty as provable gradient descent with a nontrivial learning-rate schedule.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses transformers as models not known to satisfy PL* and proposes investigating that condition for them. It also adds an interpretation that optimized PyTorch baseline implementations favor existing comparators. Earlier scheduling, small-δ, and weight-decay interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies a GeForce RTX 2060 for the ResNet/VAE experiments, gives transformer δ-GClip settings and model/data pointers, and changes the designated experiment-code repository. These are documentation and access-pointer changes; the PDFs do not establish a hardware change for retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds an explicit positioning paragraph distinguishing its approach from NTK work, supported by additional references, and cites the transformer architectures. Most of the earlier review remains intact; publication-year and venue updates for existing works are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative into separate Introduction, Results, Experiments, Related Works, Proof, and Conclusion sections. Lemmas move beside their proofs, the conclusion moves after the proofs, and prose is edited throughout. This restructuring goes beyond accommodating the new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two transformer figures, moves the Appendix B plot into the main text as Figure 3, renumbers the VAE figure, and revises captions and equation layouts. Existing plot images and the basic visual style remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The transformer experiments provide useful additional evidence of practical applicability, while the reorganized exposition and added implementation details improve accessibility. The gains remain limited by incomplete transformer training/baseline specifications and absent repeated-run uncertainty. The central method, theoretical guarantees, and original experimental evidence are unchanged.
